newsitem.title: FRANCE: Iraq return to oil market ends speculations - Qatar.
newsitem.headline: Iraq return to oil market ends speculations - Qatar.

text.p: Qatari Energy Minister Sheikh Abdullah Bin Hamad al-Attiyah, who began on Monday a 48-hour visit to Algeria, said the return of Iraq to the oil market was an element of stability, the official APS news agency said.
APS reported that al-Attiyah started his trip by visiting a gas complex located in the western city of Oran.

"The return of Iraq, whose quotas were defined by the OPEC organisation, is an element of (crude) price stability...It ends speculations which marked the previous period," APS quoted the Qatari minister as saying.
Al-Attiyah, who met the Algerian Energy Minister Amar Makhloufi, told reporters his visit was "in the framework of rich consultations between Algeria and Qatar in the fields of energy and industry."

Iraq, ostracised by world oil markets since its invasion of Kuwait six years ago, has found little difficulty in enticing foreign oil firms to rekindle old ties, Gulf-based Western traders said on Monday.
The first oil to flow out was on a tanker carrying 153,500 tonnes of Iraq's Kirkuk crude which left the Turkish Mediterranean port of Ceyhan on Monday.

Washington has given its approval for U.S. Coastal Corp to buy 60,000 barrels per day (bpd) of Iraqi Basrah crude which traders expect Coastal will take to its refinery on the Caribbean island of Aruba.
